These are the stones, the stones that speak.

Listen closely, their willing voices are weak.

Listen closely, for without fail

You'll hear a new story, an unspun tale.

"looks counterfeit" and with one assured yank, the mother-child pair was gone and another sale had failed. new york was a hotspot, spontaneous arrival should have landed in a paradise with all of Merlin's needs met. and in some respects that was the very case. even dumpster diving and rooting in garbage bins was yielding more food then a royal feast had ever let open to Merlin.

feelings snapped him to the present. returning to those lost days was a hard subject. Morgana had gone too far. a full escape had been necessary, and Arthur and all the others were most likely dead or enslaved over a ruined Camelot. but here was not Camelot, in time or place, or temporal point.

he found his days in the stifling confines of the "subway" tunnels. an invention he hadn't seen coming but was quite impressed by. he sold things on a brownish mat tucked to the side of the entrance. everywhere else that money or progress might be made asked for identification, something Merlin didn't have, and whose attempts at summoning had only created obvious fakes. he was desperate and his bones were old, and, just today, he had started selling magical items on his mat. he had only sold talking stones so far.

the flow of people that passed by him everyday were interested a bit in him, thanks to certain magical charms but was mostly a background important stream going up and down the stairwell. a man stepped forward from the stream. blue suited, younger, he cooed and awed over a vintage watch that, truthfully had cost five dollars from another street seller, and had then been aged in a time bubble.

the sale continued, but Merlin had a hole in his heart, for the city would also never accept that a grand-wizard from an old tale was walking among them. that hole solidified and filled itself somehow, when Merlin looked over the mans shoulder to see the black suited, black sunglasses wearing men, in a group of three coming down the stairs toward him. their focus, and apparent lack of focus. their cooperation, and how much they stayed separate.

he might have been wrong, looking back, but merlin, in the middle of the sale, simply dropped the watch, leaned forward grabbing the talking stones, who were actually quite friendly, and then he whispered something dark and sacred. and, then he was no longer at the station but rushing through the blackness of listless time.

maybe the next place would be different.
